name: Vanha Trokari
description: Pub, pizzeria and the village living room since forever, at the corner of Vanha Kylätie and Tiilitehtaantie. The building used to be the village store before the war.
greeting: Someone is singing a schlager slightly off key.
Lunch buffet: pea soup, again. Nobody minds.
The rooftop terrace is full of regulars.
A mölkky set leans against the door.

hello: Well look who it is. The usual?
Karaoke tonight. Don't sing Tango again.
grill_meal: Enjoy. Extra garlic, on the house.
Kiitos! Plates go back on the counter.
coffee_pulla: The pulla is from this morning. Mostly.
lottery_ticket: Good luck! The bin is right there.
Scratch it at the counter, everyone likes to watch.
work: Good shift. Grab a slice on your way out.
The oven's still hot. Same time next week?
You only burnt one pizza. Progress!
hired: You're hired! Apron's on the hook.
Welcome aboard. The dough won't knead itself.
rejected: Sorry, I just took on my cousin's kid.
Not right now. Ask me again later.
broke: Running a tab? Not with me, friend.
molkky: Over fifty, back to twenty-five. Classic.
pekki: He's alright, Pekki. Just don't ask about the dog.
Same table since 1994. We're thinking of putting up a plaque.
Thanks for keeping him company. He won't say it, but he likes it.

pekki.name: Pekki
lines: Life is like a grill sausage. You don't want to know what's in it.
I was going to be an astronaut once. Then it was Monday.
Sit down. Don't talk. This is the good part of the evening.
Another one? No. Well. Maybe one.
They say it's always darkest before the dawn. In November it's darkest all day.
You throw a dart. It hits the wall, the clock and Pekki's cap, in that order.
Bullseye! Nobody saw it. Nobody will ever believe you.
Somebody has pinned a letter from the tax office to the middle of the dartboard. It is full of holes.
The grill hisses. Rane says the fat in it is older than you.
Something smells delicious. Something else smells like 1994.
You peek into the fryer. The fryer peeks back.

actions.label: Karaoke night
actions.description: A pint and a microphone. What could go wrong?

do.message: Your voice hasn't recovered from last time. You croak through Tango and someone pulls the plug "by accident".
Same song as last time. The regulars sing along, mockingly. Rane turns the volume down a notch.
You sing a heartbroken schlager to a packed room. Someone films it.
A duet with a retired train driver. The room goes quiet, then roars.
You forget the second verse. The whole pub sings it for you.

then.message: A man in a shiny waistcoat has been listening from the back. "I play bass in the house band at the lava," he says. "We could use a voice like that."

actions.label: Play mölkky in the yard
actions.description: Throw a stick at numbered sticks. A Finnish summer must.

then.message: The regulars won't let you win twice in a week. They change the rules mid-game. Twice.

else.message: An afternoon of mölkky with the regulars.

actions.label: Buy Pekki a beer
actions.description: Pekki has held down the corner table since the nineties. He has views on life, and none of them are cheerful.

do.message: Second beer this week. Pekki starts telling the ex-dog story again, from the beginning. It is sadder the second time.
Pekki looks at you for a long time. "Don't you have anywhere else to be?" You don't. That's the sad part.
Pekki: "Summer is just three months of waiting for winter." Somehow your own life looks a lot brighter.
Pekki tells you about his ex-wife, his ex-job and his ex-dog. You walk home grateful for everything you have.
Pekki stares into his beer for an hour, then says: "Well. That's life." Deep stuff.
Pekki: "Things could be worse." Long pause. "They will be, though." You laugh until your sides hurt. He doesn't.
